reason: The hinge pins look like the parts needed to join the dragon’s wings to its body so they can move.
expectation: The wings should be hinged to the dragon’s body.

effect: The dragon now has jointed parts, ready for a linkage to move its wings.
reason: The jointed wing rods look suited to connecting the moving wings to the mechanism.
expectation: The rods should attach to the dragon’s wings.

effect: The wing rods cannot be used yet, so I should assemble more of the mechanism first.
reaction: I was surprised the rods could not attach directly to the dragon.
reason: The jointed dragon likely needs to be mounted on the cam lifter before its wings can be linked to it.
expectation: The dragon should attach to the lifter.

effect: The dragon is mounted on the lifter, so the wing rods may now be usable.
reaction: Mounting it first makes the linkage sequence clearer.
reason: The wing rods can now connect the mounted dragon to its mechanism.
expectation: The rods should connect the wings to the lifter.

effect: The wing rods now connect the follower to the hinged wings, explaining how the rising rod moves them.
reaction: Seeing how the independent pivots move the wings is satisfying.
reason: The two-humped greeting cam looks like the next part to fit to control the dragon’s wave.
expectation: The greeting cam should replace the existing cam and change the wings’ motion.

effect: The greeting cam cannot be used yet, so the linked dragon may need to be tested first.
reaction: I’m unsure why the cam is not ready to fit.
reason: The crank handle should let me test the newly linked wings.
expectation: Turning the handle should show how the dragon’s wings move with the current cam.

effect: The test shows the current cam gives one wave per turn; the two-humped cam may now be ready to change that rhythm.
reaction: The old drawing is an intriguing hint about the fair.
reason: Now that the first wave has been tested, I’ll try fitting the greeting cam again.
expectation: The new cam should make the wings wave twice per turn.

effect: The new cam is fitted, and its two rises should lift the follower twice per turn.
reaction: The cam swap makes the change in rhythm clear.
reason: The crank tested the first cam, so I’ll use it to try the new greeting.
expectation: Turning the crank should make the dragon wave twice per turn.

alternatives.reason: I could decorate the dragon first, but I want to test its new motion.

reaction: I’m surprised the new cam cannot be tested with the handle yet.
reason: The bright paper scales look like the remaining decoration for the mounted dragon.
expectation: The scales should decorate the dragon and perhaps finish it.

effect: The scales are attached, leaving the dragon decorated with its two-humped cam fitted.
reaction: The decoration worked as expected, though I still want to see the new cam in action.
reason: With the dragon decorated, I’ll try the crank again to test its greeting.

choice.combine: Dragon with a bright scaled back

expectation: Turning the crank should make the dragon wave twice per turn.

effect: The finished dragon confirms that the two-humped cam produces a double wave and can be swapped back for the single greeting.
reaction: The wave-wave rhythm is satisfying, especially after testing the first cam.

mostWorthwhile.text: Linking the wings to the follower was most worthwhile: it explained how the rods and shoulder hinges turn the follower’s rise into wing movement.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the handle immediately after fitting the new cam was frustrating because it gave no explanation for why it could not be used yet.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the wing rods could not be attached to the dragon until its body was mounted on the mechanism.

arbitrary.text: Having to add the scales before testing the second cam felt arbitrary; the result did not explain why decoration was needed first.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the cam and linkage were interesting to figure out, and Jo’s drawing made me curious about the fair in the air.
